</ul>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.2</h2>
<h3>Bug fixes</h3>
<ul>
<li>Fixed relations extraction to not interfere with Drizzle Studio.</li>
</ul>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.1</h2>
<h3>Fixed <code>drizzle-kit pull</code> bugs when using Gel extensions.</h3>
<p>Because Gel extensions create schema names containing <code>::</code> (for example, <code>ext::auth</code>), Drizzle previously handled these names incorrectly. Starting with this release, you can use Gel extensions without any problems. Here’s what you should do:</p>
<ol>
<li>Enable extensions schemas in <code>drizzle.config.ts</code></li>
</ol>
<pre lang="ts"><code>import  { defineConfig } from &quot;drizzle-kit&quot;;
<p>export default defineConfig({
dialect: 'gel',
schemaFilter: ['ext::auth', 'public']
});
</code></pre></p>
<ol start="2">
<li>
<p>Run <code>drizzle-kit pull</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Done!</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.0</h2>
<h2>Features and improvements</h2>
<h3>Enum DDL improvements</h3>
<!-- raw HTML omitted -->

| A

Updates `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` from 0.6.14 to 0.7.2
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/releases">prettier-plugin-tailwindcss's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v0.7.2</h2>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Load compatible plugins sequentially to work around race conditions in Node.js (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/412">#412</a>)</li>
<li>Fix compatibility with <code>prettier-plugin-svelte</code> when using Prettier v3.7+ (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/418">#418</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2>v0.7.1</h2>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Match against correct name of dynamic attributes when using regexes (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/410">#410</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2>v0.7.0</h2>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>Format quotes in <code>@source</code>, <code>@plugin</code>, and <code>@config</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/387">#387</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in function calls in Twig (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/358">#358</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in callable template literals (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/367">#367</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in function calls mixed with property accesses (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/367">#367</a>)</li>
<li>Support regular expression patterns for attributes (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/405">#405</a>)</li>
<li>Support regular expression patterns for function names (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/405">#405</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h3>Changed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Improved monorepo support by loading Tailwind CSS relative to the input file instead of prettier config file (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/386">#386</a>)</li>
<li>Improved monorepo support by loading v3 configs relative to the input file instead of prettier config file (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/386">#386</a>)</li>
<li>Fallback to Tailwind CSS v4 instead of v3 by default (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/390">#390</a>)</li>
<li>Don't augment global Prettier <code>ParserOptions</code> and <code>RequiredOptions</code> types (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/354">#354</a>)</li>
<li>Drop support for <code>prettier-plugin-import-sort</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/385">#385</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Handle quote escapes in LESS when sorting <code>@apply</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/392">#392</a>)</li>
<li>Fix whitespace removal inside nested concat and template expressions (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/396">#396</a>)</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
</details>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


Dependabot updated 8 packages in the `minor-and-patch` group, focusing on security patches and feature improvements.

**Key Updates:**
- **Next.js** (15.4.10→15.5.9): Includes critical security patches for CVE-2025-66478 and general security hardening
- **Drizzle ORM** (0.41.0→0.45.1): Error handling improvements with new `DrizzleQueryError`, bug fixes for `$onUpdate`, pg-native Pool detection, and sqlite blob handling
- **Drizzle Kit** (0.30.6→0.31.8): Typo fixes (`algorythm`→`algorithm`), external dependency fixes, ESM module compatibility, and enhanced studio features
- **lucide-react** (0.488.0→0.562.0): Added new icons (`toolbox`, `stone`, `fishing-hook`, `hd`, `cannabis-off`), fixed tree-shaking in react-native, improved `paint-bucket` icon
- **Prettier** (3.5.3→3.7.4): Performance improvements in doc printer, fixed TypeScript union type comment issues, LWC interpolation handling, and enhanced HTML attribute handling
- **prettier-plugin-tailwindcss** (0.6.14→0.7.2): Improved monorepo support, regex patterns for attributes/functions, Tailwind v4 default fallback, fixed Prettier v3.7+ compatibility
- **eslint-config-next** (15.1.4→15.5.9): Updated to match Next.js version with security patches
- **task-master-ai** (0.20.0→0.40.1): Major version bump with CLI performance improvements, enhanced project root detection, IDE auto-detection, watch mode, Gemini 3 support

**Security Impact:**
The Next.js updates address important security vulnerabilities. All updated packages are patch/minor versions following semver, minimizing breaking change risk.

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

### Greptile Summary

This PR enhances the profile summary card by adding markdown rendering support using `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm`. The change replaces plain text rendering with proper markdown formatting, allowing headers, lists, links, and other markdown elements in AI-generated contributor summaries to display correctly.

**What Changed:**
- Added `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` imports
- Replaced `<p>` element with `<div>` wrapped `<ReactMarkdown>` component
- Added Tailwind Typography prose classes for consistent markdown styling
- Configured prose classes to match the card's design system (custom spacing, colors for headings, dark mode support)

**Integration with Codebase:**
The summary content is AI-generated markdown from the pipeline (see `src/lib/pipelines/summarize/aiContributorSummary.ts`), which produces structured markdown with headers, lists, and links. This change ensures that markdown renders correctly in the profile summary cards, matching the pattern already used in `SummaryContent.tsx` for full summary pages.

**Security:**
`react-markdown` is safe by default - it sanitizes HTML and only renders markdown elements unless explicitly configured with `rehype-raw` plugin (which is not used here). The summary data comes from the database, populated by server-side AI generation, so there's no user-controlled input risk.

**Issue Found:**
The existing truncation logic (line 53) slices at character 300, which can break markdown syntax by cutting through links, headers, or other elements. This needs to be addressed with markdown-aware truncation or an alternative approach.

### Confidence Score: 3/5

- This PR is safe to merge with caution - the markdown rendering is implemented correctly, but the truncation logic will cause rendering issues for long lifetime summaries
- Score of 3 reflects that while the core markdown rendering implementation is correct and secure (proper use of react-markdown with GFM support, appropriate styling), there is a logic bug where the existing character-based truncation will break markdown syntax. This issue only affects lifetime summaries longer than 300 characters when not expanded. The bug won't cause crashes or security issues, but will result in malformed markdown rendering. The positive aspects are: libraries are already in dependencies, security is handled correctly by react-markdown's default sanitization, styling matches the design system, and the pattern is consistent with other markdown rendering in the codebase.
- src/components/summary-card.tsx - specifically the truncation logic at lines 48-54 which needs to be made markdown-aware

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


This PR improves database compatibility by conditionally skipping the `pgcrypto` extension installation for PGLite databases. The change leverages the existing `isRealPostgresDatabase()` detection logic to determine whether to include `pgcrypto` in the list of required extensions.

**Key changes:**
- PGLite databases now install only `vector` and `fuzzystrmatch` extensions
- Real PostgreSQL databases continue to install all three extensions including `pgcrypto`
- Eliminates unnecessary warning logs when using PGLite, which has native `gen_random_uuid()` support

The implementation follows the established pattern already used for advisory locks in the same file (lines 333 and 620), ensuring consistency. The schema files use `gen_random_uuid()` extensively (found in `room.ts`, `world.ts`, `relationship.ts`, `component.ts`, `participant.ts`), which works natively in PGLite without requiring the `pgcrypto` extension.

<h3>Confidence Score: 5/5</h3>


- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk
- The change is a simple, well-targeted fix that follows existing patterns in the codebase. It reuses the `isRealPostgresDatabase()` method that's already used elsewhere in the same file for advisory locks. The logic is sound: PGLite has native `gen_random_uuid()` support and doesn't need the `pgcrypto` extension, while real PostgreSQL databases continue to receive all required extensions. The change eliminates unnecessary warning logs without affecting functionality, and there's no risk of breaking existing behavior since the extension installation uses `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS` with error handling that continues on failure.
- No files require special attention

|----------|----------|
| packages/plugin-sql/src/runtime-migrator/runtime-migrator.ts | Conditionally skips `pgcrypto` extension installation for PGLite, which natively supports `gen_random_uuid()` |

sequenceDiagram

    Migrator->>EnvCheck: Get POSTGRES_URL/DATABASE_URL

    alt Real PostgreSQL

<!-- /greptile_comment -->69:T13fa,## Summary
Fixes #228 

Stats files (`data/elizaos_eliza/stats/day/stats_*.json`) always had `summary: null` for contributors, even when summaries existed in the database. This was due to a pipeline ordering issue.

## Problem

The workflow had stats being exported BEFORE contributor summaries were generated:

1. `ingest-export` job → exports stats files (summaries don't exist yet → `summary: null`)
2. `generate-summaries` job → creates contributor summaries
3. Stats files never re-exported to include summaries

## Solution

Added a re-export step after summary generation completes (line 293):

```yaml
- name: Re-export stats with contributor summaries
  run: bun run pipeline export${{ env.start_date_arg }}${{ env.end_date_arg }}${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && ' --days 2' || '' }} -f
```

**Behavior:**
- **Scheduled runs**: Re-export last 2 days only (`--days 2`)
- **Manual runs with date range**: Re-export the specified date range
- **Manual runs without dates**: Re-export everything missing

## Why Three Export Steps?

The workflow now has three export commands, each serving a purpose:

1. **Line 119**: Export everything missing (respects manual date ranges)
2. **Line 120**: Force re-export last 2 days for data completeness (April 2025 "overlap" feature)
3. **Line 293 (NEW)**: Force re-export WITH summaries after generation

This preserves the existing "overlap" safety feature while ensuring summaries are included when available.

## Test Plan
- [ ] CI checks pass
- [ ] Manual workflow run to verify summary inclusion
- [ ] Verify scheduled runs only re-export 2 days
- [ ] Verify manual runs with date range respect inputs

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- /greptile_comment -->6b:Td49,This PR adds validation to the `ensureDir` function to prevent unclear ENOENT errors when an empty directory path is provided.

## Problem

When `ensureDir` was called with an empty string or whitespace-only path, it would attempt to execute `fs.mkdir('', { recursive: true })`, which results in the cryptic error:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir
```

This error message doesn't clearly indicate that the problem is an empty directory path.

## Solution

Added validation in the `ensureDir` function to check if the path is empty or contains only whitespace before attempting any filesystem operations.

## Changes

- Added validation: `if (!dirPath || dirPath.trim() === '')`
- Throws clear error: `"Directory path cannot be empty"`
- Validation happens before `existsSync` and `mkdir` calls

## Benefits

1. **Clearer error messages**: Users now get a descriptive error instead of ENOENT
2. **Earlier failure**: Fails fast before attempting filesystem operations
3. **Better debugging**: Makes it obvious when configuration results in empty paths

## Related Issues

This fix helps address issues like #5607 where directory creation fails with unclear errors.

## Testing

The validation is straightforward and will throw an error whenever `ensureDir` is called with an empty or whitespace-only string, preventing the ENOENT error from occurring.

<!-- greptile_comment -->

    CLI2->>C: No direct usage
    
    Note over ET,C: Compatibility Check
    ET-->>C: Peer dependency mismatch risk
    C-->>PJ: May need upgrade to 14.x
```

<!-- /greptile_comment -->70:T37e2,Bumps [date-fns](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns) from 3.6.0 to 4.1.0.
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/releases">date-fns's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v4.1.0</h2>
<p>This release adds time zone support to format functions (that I somehow missed when working on the feature) and fixes a few bugs.</p>
<p>Make sure also upgrade <code>TZDate</code> to v1.0.2 as it <a href="https://github.com/date-fns/tz/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v102---2024-09-14">includes a bunch of critical bug fixes</a>.</p>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Fixed internal <code>constructFrom</code> throwing an exception on <code>null</code> arguments. While <code>null</code> isn't allowed, the functions should rather return <code>Invalid Date</code> or <code>NaN</code> in such cases. See <a href="https://redirect.github.com/date-fns/date-fns/issues/3885">#3885</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>Added missing time zone support to <code>format</code>, <code>formatISO</code>, <code>formatISO9075</code>, <code>formatRelative</code> and <code>formatRFC3339</code>. See <a href="https://redirect.github.com/date-fns/date-fns/issues/3886">#3886</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>v4.0.0</h2>
<p>I have great news! First, ten years after its release, date-fns finally gets first-class time zone support.</p>
<p>Another great news is that there aren't many breaking changes in this release. All of them are type-related and will affect only those explicitly using internal date-fns types. Finally, it has been less than a year since the last major release, which is an improvement over the previous four years between v2 and v3. I plan on keeping the pace and minimizing breaking changes moving forward.</p>
<p><a href="https://blog.date-fns.org/v40-with-time-zone-support/">Read more about the release in the announcement blog post</a>.</p>
<p>- <a href="https://twitter.com/kossnocorp"><code>Sasha @​kossnocorp</code></a></p>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Added time zones support via <a href="https://github.com/date-fns/tz"><code>@date-fns/tz</code></a>'s <code>TZDate</code> class and <code>tz</code> helper function. See its <a href="https://github.com/date-fns/tz">README</a> for the details about the API.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>All relevant functions now accept the context <code>in</code> option, which allows to specify the time zone to make the calculations in. If the function also returns a date, it will be in the specified time zone:</p>
<pre lang="ts"><code>import { addDays, startOfDay } from &quot;date-fns&quot;;
import { tz } from &quot;@date-fns/tz&quot;;
<p>startOfDay(addDays(Date.now(), 5, { in: tz(&quot;Asia/Singapore&quot;) }));<br />
//=&gt; &quot;2024-09-16T00:00:00.000+08:00&quot;<br />
</code></pre></p>
<p>In the example, <code>addDays</code> will get the current date and time in Singapore and add 5 days to it. <code>startOfDay</code> will inherit the date type and return the start of the day in Singapore.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3>Changed</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>The function arguments, as well as <code>Interval</code>'s <code>start</code> and <code>end</code>, now can be of different types, allowing you to mix <code>UTCDate</code>, <code>TZDate</code>, <code>Date</code>, and other extensions, as well as primitives (strings and numbers).</p>
<p>The functions will normalize these values, make calculations, and return the result in the same type, preventing any bugs caused by the discrepancy. If passed, the type will be inferred from the context <code>in</code> option or the first encountered argument object type. The <code>Interval</code>'s <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> will be considered separately, starting from <code>start</code>.</p>
<p>In the given example, the result will be in the <code>TZDate</code> as the first argument is a number, and the <code>start</code> takes precedence over the <code>end</code>.</p>
<pre lang="ts"><code>clamp(Date.now(), {
  start: new TZDate(start, &quot;Asia/Singapore&quot;),
  end: new UTCDate(),
</code></pre>
</li>
</ul>
<!-- raw HTML omitted -->
</blockquote>
<p>... (truncated)</p>

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


Dependency upgrade bumping `date-fns` from v3.6.0 to v4.1.0. This is a major version update that introduces first-class time zone support and several improvements.

Key changes in date-fns v4:
- Added time zone support via `TZDate` class and `in` option for context
- Functions can now accept mixed date types (`UTCDate`, `TZDate`, `Date`, primitives)
- Fixed `constructFrom` bug with null arguments
- Breaking changes are primarily type-related affecting internal date-fns types only

The codebase primarily uses:
- `addDays`, `subDays`, `addMonths`, `differenceInDays`, `formatDate` from `date-fns`
- `UTCDate` from `@date-fns/utc` (separate package, unaffected)
- All usage patterns appear compatible with v4 API

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>


- This PR is safe to merge with low risk
- This is an automated dependency upgrade to a major version with mostly backward-compatible changes. The breaking changes are type-related and don't affect the function APIs used in this codebase. The codebase uses basic date manipulation functions (addDays, subDays, formatDate) which have stable APIs. The project already uses `@date-fns/utc` package which is separate and unaffected by this upgrade.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR updates `commander` from v12.1.0 to v14.0.2, a major version bump that includes breaking changes and new features.

**Key Changes:**
- Commander v14 now requires Node.js v20 or higher (breaking change)
- Adds support for option/command grouping in help output
- Adds support for unescaped negative numbers as arguments
- Multiple bug fixes and code quality improvements

**Compatibility Assessment:**
The codebase uses `@commander-js/extra-typings` (already at v14.0.0) and imports from it in `cli/analyze-pipeline.ts:29` and `cli/data-sync.ts:15`. The project runs on Bun (latest version in CI workflows), which supports Node.js v20+ APIs, so this update should be compatible.

**No Code Changes Needed:**
The usage patterns in the CLI scripts are straightforward and don't use deprecated APIs. The update should work without modifications.

# Background

## What does this PR do?
Remove unnecessary manual acquire/release client from PgPool. Official docs stated that using PgPool's query directly is perfectly fine: https://node-postgres.com/apis/pool#poolquery
The only exception is when we incorrectly run transaction against PgPool, which is not the case since drizzle already handle that for us

## What kind of change is this?
Bug fixes (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Why are we doing this? Any context or related work?
We encountered random `Client was closed and not queryable` error when running db query. It only happened within our repository code, never on eliza's core db access. After some digging we found [pg/adapter.ts](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/df5758034ab9843e913b1cc7b327f4dad8bb2e0f/packages/plugin-sql/src/pg/adapter.ts#L84) assigning runtime.db to individual PoolClient

By re-assign `runtime.db` to a single connection from connection pool, that connection can get dropped even though it was referenced elsewhere, which would cause intermittent error when implementing database access following the Repository pattern guide73:T5109,Bumps the minor-and-patch group with 2 updates in the / directory: [prettier](https://github.com/prettier/prettier) and [task-master-ai](https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master).

</ul>

<p><a href="https://redirect.github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/pull/1566">#1566</a> <a href="https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/commit/3cc6174b471fc1ea7f12955095d0d35b4dc5904c"><code>3cc6174</code></a> Thanks <a href="https://github.com/bjcoombs"><code>@​bjcoombs</code></a>! - Fix race condition when multiple Claude Code windows write to tasks.json simultaneously</p>
<ul>
<li>Add cross-process file locking to prevent concurrent write collisions</li>
<li>Implement atomic writes using temp file + rename pattern to prevent partial writes</li>
<li>Re-read file inside lock to get current state, preventing lost updates from stale snapshots</li>
<li>Add stale lock detection and automatic cleanup (10-second timeout)</li>
<li>Export <code>withFileLock</code> and <code>withFileLockSync</code> utilities for use by other modules</li>
</ul>
<p>This fix prevents data loss that could occur when multiple Task Master instances (e.g., multiple Claude Code windows) access the same tasks.json file concurrently.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="https://redirect.github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/pull/1576">#1576</a> <a href="https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/commit/097c8edcb0ca065218e9b51758ad370ac7475f1a"><code>097c8ed</code></a> Thanks <a href="https://github.com/Crunchyman-ralph"><code>@​Crunchyman-ralph</code></a>! - Improve loop command error handling and use dangerously-skip-permissions</p>

import * as prettierPluginEstree from &quot;prettier/plugins/estree&quot;;

prettierPluginEstree.printers.estree; //=&gt; any</p>
<p>// Prettier 3.8.1
prettierPluginEstree.printers.estree; //=&gt; Printer
prettierPluginEstree.printers[&quot;estree-json&quot;]; //=&gt; Printer

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


This automated Dependabot PR upgrades `actions/upload-pages-artifact` from v3 to v4, which introduces a potentially breaking change: **dotfiles are now excluded from artifacts by default**.

Key considerations:
- The repository contains a `.nojekyll` file in the root directory that is critical for GitHub Pages deployment (prevents Jekyll from ignoring files with underscores like Next.js's `_next` directory)
- The workflow copies the `out` directory (Next.js build output) but there's no explicit step showing `.nojekyll` being copied into `out/`
- If `.nojekyll` is not included in the artifact, the GitHub Pages site may break
- The v4 release notes explicitly state that if dotfiles are needed, users should create their own artifact rather than using this action

Verify that `.nojekyll` either:
1. Gets copied into the `out/` directory during the Next.js build process, OR
2. Is explicitly copied before the upload step, OR  
3. Is not actually needed (though this would be unusual for Next.js static exports)

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>


- This PR has moderate risk due to the v4 breaking change around dotfile exclusion
- The version bump itself is straightforward, but v4 excludes dotfiles by default which could break GitHub Pages deployment if `.nojekyll` is not properly included in the artifact. This needs verification before merge.
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` - verify `.nojekyll` handling before merge

| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|
| .github/workflows/deploy.yml | Version bump from v3 to v4 for `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, no logic changes |

    participant Deploy as deploy-pages@v4

    Checkout-->>GHA: Repository files (includes .nojekyll)
    
    GHA->>Build: Run bun build
    Build->>Build: Generate static files to out/
    Note over Build: Question: Is .nojekyll copied to out/?
    Build-->>GHA: out/ directory ready
    
    GHA->>GHA: Copy data/ into out/
    GHA->>GHA: Copy out/data/api to out/api
    
    GHA->>UploadV4: Upload artifact from out/
    Note over UploadV4: v4: Excludes dotfiles by default
    Note over UploadV4: Breaking change from v3
    UploadV4->>UploadV4: Filter out .nojekyll (if present)
    UploadV4-->>GHA: Artifact uploaded (without dotfiles)
    
    GHA->>Deploy: Deploy artifact
    Deploy->>Pages: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    
    alt .nojekyll missing
        Pages->>Pages: Jekyll processing enabled
        Pages->>Pages: Ignore _next/ directory
        Note over Pages: DEPLOYMENT BROKEN
    else .nojekyll present
        Pages->>Pages: Jekyll processing disabled
        Pages->>Pages: Serve all files correctly
        Note over Pages: Deployment successful
    end

## Executive Summary (2-3 sentences)
January marked a pivotal month of strategic planning, as we defined a clear and ambitious roadmap for the next phase of ElizaOS. This effort focused on building a robust public agent ecosystem and enhancing the user experience, all while delivering key backend performance improvements to ensure the platform remains fast and reliable.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

-   **Defining the Next Generation of Public Agents**
    The strategic focus this month was on laying the groundwork for a vibrant, open ecosystem where users can discover, share, and build upon AI agents. This initiative is central to our mission of fostering decentralized and collaborative intelligence.
    -   A comprehensive roadmap was established in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) to create a public agent discovery platform ([#6302](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6302)), allow users to fork and customize existing agents ([#6305](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6305)), and enable knowledge sharing between them ([#6303](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6303)).

-   **Improving Platform Performance and Reliability**
    To support future growth and ensure a smooth user experience, we prioritized work on optimizing our core infrastructure. A faster, more stable platform is essential for agent performance and user retention.
    -   The core message service in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) was significantly refactored, resulting in faster execution for multi-step agent actions ([#6263](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/6263)).
    -   Work began to resolve a bug in the SQL plugin to prevent incorrect behavior and improve reliability ([#6316](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/6316)).

-   **Refining the User Experience and Growth Strategy**
    Alongside backend planning, we outlined key improvements to the user interface and explored new strategies for sustainable growth. These efforts aim to make the platform more intuitive for new users and support our long-term development.
    -   New plans were created in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) to refine the user interface, including adjustments to the chat experience ([#6310](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6310), [#6311](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6311)) and fixing interaction bugs ([#6322](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6322)).
    -   Strategies for platform growth were proposed, such as adjusting message limits for guest users ([#6312](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6312)) and modifying initial credit offerings ([#6315](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/6315)).

<img width="1608" height="1764" alt="Image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af7d141b-295e-4d54-ba78-d9455a1f61e1" />83:T542,## Description

Integrate N8N workflow engine as the primary automation layer for Eliza App. N8N provides pre-built nodes for Gmail, Notion, Calendar, and hundreds of other services.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] N8N plugin from V2 branch working in cloud
- [ ] Agent can generate workflow JSONs via natural language
- [ ] Workflows can be stored per user/tenant
- [ ] Execution via [N8N.io](<http://N8N.io>) or self-hosted execution server
- [ ] Query available nodes and expose to agent

## Technical Notes

**From today's meeting (Shaw):**

* N8N plugin already exists in V2 branch - generates JSON workflows
* "We get every single thing" - Gmail, Notion, Reddit, literally every connector exists
* Two parts: (1) Generate JSON workflows (no sandbox needed), (2) Execute via N8N server
* Can use [N8N.io](<http://N8N.io>) hosted execution initially, self-host later for cost optimization
* Workflow generation is just JSON - can happen serverlessly
* Also need to pull in pre-existing workflows from GitHub (many already exist)
* "I really think we could get this done today" - Shaw

## Architecture

1. User says "check my gmail every morning"
2. Agent generates N8N workflow JSON
3. Agent requests OAuth credentials if needed
4. Workflow submitted to N8N execution server
5. Results returned to user

  "generatedAt": "2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z",
  "contentFormat": "markdown",
  "content": "No activity recorded for January 1, 2026."
}
```

## Root Cause

[`generateOverallSummaryForInterval()`](https://github.com/elizaOS/elizaos.github.io/blob/main/src/lib/pipelines/summarize/generateOverallSummary.ts#L70-L76) returns `null` when no repository summaries exist:

```typescript
const repoSummaries = await getAllRepoSummariesForInterval(interval);
if (repoSummaries.length === 0) {
  intervalLogger?.debug(
    `No repository summaries found for ${intervalType} of ${startDate}, skipping overall summary generation.`,
  );
  return null; // ← This causes the 404
}
```

## Evidence

```bash
# Jan 1 had ZERO activity (New Year's Day)
$ sqlite3 data/db.sqlite "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw_pull_requests WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2026-01-01';"
0

$ sqlite3 data/db.sqlite "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM raw_issues WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2026-01-01';"
0

# Database has monthly summary but NO daily summary
$ sqlite3 data/db.sqlite "SELECT date, interval_type, LENGTH(summary) FROM overall_summaries WHERE date = '2026-01-01';"
2026-01-01|month|4320
```

## Solution

Always generate a summary, even when `repoSummaries.length === 0`:

```typescript
const repoSummaries = await getAllRepoSummariesForInterval(interval);

// Generate summary even if no repo summaries exist
const summary = repoSummaries.length > 0
  ? await generateOverallSummary(
      repoSummaries,
      aiSummaryConfig,
      { startDate },
      intervalType as RepoIntervalType,
    )
  : `No activity recorded for ${intervalType} of ${startDate}.`;

if (\!summary) {
  intervalLogger?.debug(
    `Overall summary generation resulted in no content for ${startDate}, skipping storage.`,
  );
  return;
}

// Store and export the summary...
```

## Impact

- API consumers can't distinguish between "no data" and "endpoint not generated"
- 404s break API contract that promises daily summaries
- Inconsistent API behavior (some days exist, others don't)
- Downstream tools must handle unexpected 404s

## Design Philosophy

Per the API documentation:
> "404 responses indicate artifacts not yet published."

But this should mean "pipeline hasn't run yet", NOT "no activity that day". If the pipeline runs daily, every day should have a summary—even if it says "no activity."

## References

- API Documentation: https://elizaos.github.io/api
- Generation code: `src/lib/pipelines/summarize/generateOverallSummary.ts:70-76`
- OpenAPI spec: https://elizaos.github.io/openapi.json87:Tabf,## Problem

The following API endpoints return 404 on production:
- `/api/index.json`
- `/api/contributors/{username}/profile.json` (all 1,433 contributor profiles)

Meanwhile, these endpoints work fine:
- `/api/leaderboard-*.json` ✅
- `/api/summaries/**` ✅

## Root Cause

The `run-pipelines.yml` workflow doesn't set the `SITE_URL` environment variable when running `bun run pipeline export-leaderboard`.

Without `SITE_URL`, the following functions skip exporting:
- [`exportAPIIndex()`](https://github.com/elizaOS/elizaos.github.io/blob/main/src/lib/pipelines/export/exportLeaderboardAPI.ts#L1180-L1184) - skips with warning "SITE_URL not configured"
- [`exportAllUserProfiles()`](https://github.com/elizaOS/elizaos.github.io/blob/main/src/lib/pipelines/export/exportLeaderboardAPI.ts#L1078-L1081) - skips with info "Skipping user profiles: SITE_URL not configured"

The files ARE generated locally during `deploy.yml` build (12MB of contributor profiles), but they're generated too late—after the pipelines have already run.

## Evidence

```bash
# Files exist locally after build
$ ls -lh out/api/
drwxr-xr-x 1435 jin jin   36M contributors/  # ← 404 on production
-rw-r--r--    1 jin jin  4.0K index.json      # ← 404 on production
-rw-r--r--    1 jin jin  2.6M leaderboard-lifetime.json  # ✅ works
-rw-r--r--    1 jin jin   34K leaderboard-monthly.json   # ✅ works
drwxr-xr-x    5 jin jin  4.0K summaries/      # ✅ works
```

```bash
# Production only has these
$ curl -s https://elizaos.github.io/api/ | grep href
href="summaries/"
href="leaderboard-lifetime.json"
href="leaderboard-monthly.json"
href="leaderboard-weekly.json"
```

## Solution

Add SITE_URL to `run-pipelines.yml` env section:

```yaml
env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
  PIPELINE_DATA_BRANCH: "_data"
  DATA_DIR: "data"
  SITE_URL: ${{ secrets.SITE_URL || 'https://elizaos.github.io' }}  # ← Add this
  PIPELINE_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ secrets.PIPELINE_CONFIG_FILE || 'config/example.json' }}
```

Or detect it dynamically like `deploy.yml` does:
```yaml
- name: Determine site URL
  id: site-config
  run: |
    if [[ "${{ github.event.repository.name }}" == *.github.io ]]; then
      echo "site_url=https://${{ github.repository_owner }}.github.io" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    fi
```

- 12MB of contributor profile data not accessible via API
- API discovery endpoint (`/api/index.json`) returns 404

**1. Describe the bug**
The `@elizaos/plugin-telegram` crashes when a user uploads an image "as a photo" via the Telegram client (as opposed to sending it "as a file"). The internal `processImage` function within the plugin's `messageManager.ts` calls `runtime.useModel(ModelType.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION, ...)` with incorrect parameters. It passes a raw string (`imageUrl`) as the second argument, but the `useModel` function for `IMAGE_DESCRIPTION` expects an object (`ImageDescriptionParams`). This results in a `TypeError: paramsObj is not an Object.` which halts all further message processing.

**2. To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  Set up an ElizaOS project with `@elizaos/plugin-telegram`.
2.  Ensure a model provider that can handle `ModelType.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION` is configured (e.g., `@elizaos/plugin-google-genai` with `GOOGLE_IMAGE_MODEL` set).
3.  Start the ElizaOS server (`elizaos dev`).
4.  In a Telegram chat with the bot, send an image by selecting it as a "Photo" (using the compressed/gallery option), not as a "File".
5.  Observe the server logs. The application will throw a `TypeError` and likely fail to respond to the message.

**3. Expected behavior**
The `processImage` function should not crash. It should successfully call `runtime.useModel` with the correct parameters, receive an image description, and create a valid `attachment` object that can be passed to the main message processing pipeline.

**4. Logs**
Here is the relevant stack trace from the crash:
```
❌ Error processing image: TypeError: paramsObj is not an Object. (evaluating '"prompt" in paramsObj')
      at useModel (.../node_modules/@elizaos/core/dist/node/index.node.js:48866:53)
      at processImage (.../node_modules/@elizaos/plugin-telegram/dist/index.js:207:59)
      at async processMessage (.../node_modules/@elizaos/plugin-telegram/dist/index.js:431:36)
      ...```

**5. Suggested Fix**
The call to `useModel` inside the `processImage` function in `plugin-telegram/src/messageManager.ts` needs to be updated to match the expected `ImageDescriptionParams` interface.

The current implementation is:
```typescript
const { title, description } = await this.runtime.useModel(
  ModelType.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION,
  imageUrl
);
```
This should be changed to pass an object, and it should also include the user's caption as the prompt for better contextual analysis:
```typescript
const { title, description } = await this.runtime.useModel(
  ModelType.IMAGE_DESCRIPTION,
  { 
    imageUrl: imageUrl,
    prompt: message.caption || "Describe this image." 
  }
);
```

This change aligns the function call with the core `@elizaos/core` type definitions and resolves the `TypeError`.8e:T622,## Context

```markdown
BEFORE (Vulnerable - Race Condition)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

   Request 1 ──┐
   Request 2 ──┼──▶ CHECK balance ≥ $0.02? ──▶ ✅ YES ──┐
   Request 3 ──┤         (all pass)                     │
   Request N ──┘                                        │
                                                        ▼
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │           STREAMING (10+ sec)            │
                         │         No lock held on balance          │
                         └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                        │
                                                        ▼
   All requests ──────────────────────────────▶ DEDUCT $0.02 each
                                                        │
                                                        ▼
                                            💥 Balance goes NEGATIVE
                                            or deductions FAIL silently


AFTER (Fixed - Atomic Reservation)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

   Request 1 ──┐         ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
   Request 2 ──┼──▶      │  ATOMIC: SELECT FOR UPDATE + DEDUCT    │
   Request 3 ──┤         │  (PostgreSQL row lock on org balance)   │
   Request N ──┘         └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                            │
              ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
              │                             │                             │
              ▼                             ▼                             ▼
        Request 1                     Request 2-N                   
        ✅ RESERVED                   ❌ 402 REJECTED
        $0.03 (with buffer)           "Insufficient credits"
              │                             
              ▼                             
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │           STREAMING (10+ sec)            │
   │         Credits already deducted         │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  RECONCILE: actual cost = $0.012        │
   │  REFUND: $0.03 - $0.012 = $0.018        │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
              │
              ▼
        ✅ Balance NEVER negative

return `${pr.repository}#${pr.number} ...`;

9b:T836,## Problem

Contributor summaries are always `null` in exported stats files (e.g., `data/elizaos_eliza/stats/day/stats_2026-01-20.json`), even when contributor summaries exist in the database.

## Root Cause

Pipeline ordering issue in `.github/workflows/run-pipelines.yml`:

1. **Job 1: `ingest-export`** (lines 60-146)
   - Runs `bun run pipeline export` 
   - Generates stats files with `topContributors` array
   - At this point, NO contributor summaries exist → all `summary` fields are `null`

2. **Job 2: `generate-summaries`** (lines 148-340) 
   - Runs AFTER job 1 completes
   - Generates contributor summaries and stores them in database
   - Stats files are NEVER re-exported to pick up the new summaries

## Evidence

```bash
# Stats file generated before summaries exist:
$ cat data/elizaos_eliza/stats/day/stats_2026-01-16.json | jq '.topContributors[0]'
{
  "username": "0xbbjoker",
  ...
  "summary": null  # ← Always null
}

# But summary exists in database:
$ sqlite3 data/db.sqlite "SELECT LENGTH(summary) FROM user_summaries WHERE username = '0xbbjoker' AND date = '2026-01-16' AND interval_type = 'day';"
166  # ← Summary has 166 characters
```

## Solution

Re-export stats files after contributor summaries are generated. Options:

### Option 1: Add export step to generate-summaries job (Recommended)
After line 261 in `.github/workflows/run-pipelines.yml`, add:
```yaml
- name: Re-export stats with contributor summaries
  run: bun run pipeline export --days 7 -f
```

### Option 2: Separate job with dependency
Create a third job that runs after `generate-summaries` to re-export stats.

## Impact

- All contributor summaries in stats files are missing, even though they exist in the database
- Frontend/API consumers see `summary: null` instead of rich contributor activity descriptions
- Affects all interval types (day, week, month)

## Related Files

- `.github/workflows/run-pipelines.yml`
- `src/lib/pipelines/export/queries.ts:114-165` (`getTopContributors` function)
- `src/lib/pipelines/export/exportRepoStats.ts:17-97` (`exportRepoStatsForInterval` function)9c:T783,# Untracked repositories table has 2x more columns than tracked repositories

## Current State

**Tracked repos (8 columns):**
- Core: `repoId`, `owner`, `name`, `description`
- Metrics: `stars`, `forks`
- Timestamps: `lastFetchedAt`, `lastUpdated`

**Untracked repos (18 columns):**
- Core: `repoId`, `owner`, `name`, `description`
- Metrics: `stars`, `forks`, `watchers`
- Metadata: `isArchived`, `primaryLanguage`
- Timestamps: `lastUpdatedAt`, `lastPushedAt`, `lastFetchedAt`
- Activity: `openPrCount`, `mergedPrCount`, `closedUnmergedPrCount`, `openIssueCount`, `closedIssueCount`
- Score: `activityScore`

## Issue

The "lightweight" untracked repos table has **18 columns** vs **8 columns** in tracked repos (2.25x more).

## Why It Happened

**Tracked repos**: Normalized architecture
- Minimal `repositories` table
- Separate `rawPullRequests`, `rawIssues`, `rawCommits` tables with full details

**Untracked repos**: Denormalized architecture  
- Everything in one table (no separate PR/issue tables)
- Stores counts and scores directly

## Potential Optimization

Could reduce to **9 essential columns**:
```sql
repoId, owner, name, description,
stars, forks,
lastUpdatedAt,  -- for delta detection
activityScore,  -- pre-computed
lastFetchedAt
```

**Trade-offs:**
- ✅ Simpler schema (9 vs 18 columns)
- ✅ Matches tracked repos complexity
- ❌ Lose tri-split PR/issue counts in DB (would need to recompute for UI)
- ❌ Lose metadata (language, archived status)

## Questions

1. Do we need tri-split counts stored, or can we compute on-the-fly?
2. Is `primaryLanguage` valuable for filtering/display?
3. Is `isArchived` needed or already filtered during ingestion?

## Non-Goal

This is not urgent - the denormalized approach works fine. Just documenting for future consideration.

## References

- Schema: `src/lib/data/schema.ts` lines 859-896
- Discovery: `src/lib/pipelines/discoverUntrackedRepos.ts`
9d:T1435,## Problem Statement

We currently have 43 tracked repositories and 286 untracked repositories across the `elizaos` and `elizaos-plugins` organizations. The `config/example.json` file that determines which repos get full tracking (PRs, issues, commits, contributors, scoring) is manually maintained.

**Challenges:**
- Some tracked repos haven't been updated in months (low activity)
- Active untracked repos could benefit from full contributor analytics
- Manual config updates are time-consuming and error-prone
- No systematic way to identify promotion/demotion candidates

## Research Summary

Comprehensive research explored 6 strategies for automating config management. Full details in plan document: `/home/jin/.claude/plans/ticklish-finding-kitten.md`

### Strategy Comparison

| Strategy | Automation | Risk | Complexity | Effort | API Impact |
|----------|-----------|------|------------|--------|------------|
| 1. Threshold Auto | High | Medium | Medium | 8-12h | Reduces tracked |
| 2. Manual Review Dashboard | Low | None | Low | 8-11h | None |
| 3. Tiered Tracking | High | Medium | High | 21-27h | Reduces overall |
| 4. Adaptive Refresh | Medium | Low | Low | 6-9h | Reduces refresh |
| **5. CI/CD PR** ⭐ | Medium | Low | Medium | **9-13h** | Reduces tracked |
| 6. Hybrid Auto/Manual | Medium | Low | Medium | 10-14h | Reduces tracked |

### Recommended Approach

**Short-term (Quick Win):** Strategy 2 - Manual Review Dashboard
- Generate weekly report of stale tracked repos and active untracked repos
- Dashboard UI for human review
- Low risk, immediate value
- **Effort: 8-11 hours**

**Long-term (Automation):** Strategy 5 - CI/CD Automated Config PRs
- Weekly GitHub Actions workflow evaluates repos
- Auto-generates PRs with promotion/demotion recommendations
- Rich context for human review (activity trends, contributor counts, recent commits)
- Requires approval before merging
- **Effort: 9-13 hours**

### Key Technical Findings

**Reusable Code Identified:**
- ✅ `calculateActivityScore()` - Already exists in `src/lib/pipelines/untracked/mutations.ts`
- ✅ Activity score formula: log-scale stars/watchers, weighted PRs/issues, recency bonus
- ✅ Database batch operations pattern
- ✅ Time interval filtering utilities
- ✅ GitHub CLI PR creation patterns
- ✅ Config schema validation (Zod)

**Activity Score Formula:**
```typescript
activityScore = baseScore * archivePenalty

baseScore =
  log(stars + 1) * 1.0 +          // Log-scaled popularity
  log(watchers + 1) * 1.5 +       // Stronger engagement
  openPrCount * 3 +               // Active development (highest weight)
  mergedPrCount * 2 +             // Productive activity
  closedUnmergedPrCount * 1 +     // Engagement
  openIssueCount * 2 +            // Active discussions
  closedIssueCount * 1 +          // Maintenance
  recencyBonus                    // Max 14 points, decays over 14 days

archivePenalty = 0.5 if archived, else 1.0
```

### Implementation Outline (Strategy 5)

**Phase 1: Core Evaluation**
- Calculate activity scores for tracked repos (reuse existing formula)
- Build evaluation logic with hysteresis thresholds
- CLI command for testing: `bun run pipeline evaluate-tracking`

**Phase 2: PR Automation**
- Config update logic (read/modify `config/example.json`)
- Rich markdown PR description with activity details
- Preview comments showing recent contributor activity
- GitHub Actions workflow (weekly schedule + manual trigger)

**Phase 3: Refinement**
- Threshold tuning based on initial recommendations
- Testing with various scenarios
- Documentation and runbook for reviewing PRs

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


Introduces `dynamicPromptExecFromState()` across Python, Rust, and TypeScript runtimes to provide schema-driven prompt execution with context validation via UUID codes. The implementation detects when LLMs truncate output due to limited context windows by injecting validation codes at strategic positions (start/middle/end or per-field). Supports four validation levels (0=trusted to 3=full), exponential backoff retries, and optional validation-aware streaming via `ValidationStreamExtractor`.

**Key changes:**
- Cross-language API consistency for dynamic prompt execution with state injection
- Validation code system to detect context overflow (4 levels: trusted, progressive, checkpoint, full)
- Streaming integration with progressive validation and retry support
- Schema-based structured output parsing (XML/JSON) with required field validation
- Performance metrics tracking per model+schema combination (TypeScript only)
- Comprehensive type definitions (`SchemaRow`, `RetryBackoffConfig`, `StreamEvent`)

**Critical issues in Python implementation:**
- Callable prompt invocation wraps state incorrectly (`{"state": state}` vs direct state access)
- Template substitution assumes `state.values` has dynamic attributes accessible via `dir()`, incompatible with protobuf State
- XML parsing regex `\w+` won't match validation field names with underscores like `code_text_start`

**Minor issues:**
- Rust template rendering uses basic string replacement instead of full Handlebars compiler
- TypeScript `_smartRetryContext` deletion during retry loop prevents reuse on subsequent attempts
- ValidationStreamExtractor abort handling may leave inconsistent state

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>


- Python implementation has runtime errors that will break production usage; TypeScript and Rust implementations are safer but need testing
- Score reflects critical logical errors in Python (3 bugs that will cause runtime failures), plus architecture differences across languages. TypeScript implementation is most complete with metrics and full Handlebars support. Python bugs must be fixed before merge to avoid breaking callers.
- `packages/python/elizaos/runtime.py` requires immediate fixes for callable invocation, state.values access pattern, and XML regex. Test the Python implementation thoroughly before merging.

<h3>Sequence Diagram</h3>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Runtime
    participant ValidationExtractor
    participant LLM
    participant Parser

    Client->>Runtime: dynamicPromptExecFromState(state, schema, options)
    
    Note over Runtime: Generate validation codes<br/>(UUID snippets)
    
    Runtime->>Runtime: Build extended schema<br/>with validation fields
    
    Runtime->>Runtime: Inject codes into prompt<br/>(initial, middle, end)
    
    Runtime->>Runtime: Compile template with<br/>Handlebars/state values
    
    alt Streaming enabled
        Runtime->>ValidationExtractor: Create extractor<br/>(level, schema, codes)
    end
    
    loop Retry attempts (0 to maxRetries)
        Runtime->>LLM: Generate text with prompt
        
        alt Streaming
            loop Stream chunks
                LLM-->>ValidationExtractor: chunk
                ValidationExtractor->>ValidationExtractor: Extract field content
                ValidationExtractor->>ValidationExtractor: Check per-field codes<br/>(level 0-1)
                ValidationExtractor-->>Client: Stream validated content
            end
        else Non-streaming
            LLM-->>Runtime: Complete response
        end
        
        Runtime->>Runtime: Clean response<br/>(remove <think> tags)
        
        Runtime->>Parser: Parse XML/JSON response
        Parser-->>Runtime: Parsed fields object
        
        Runtime->>Runtime: Normalize structured response
        
        alt Validation level 0-1
            loop For each field with code
                Runtime->>Runtime: Check start/end codes match
            end
        else Validation level 2-3
            Runtime->>Runtime: Check checkpoint codes<br/>(one_initial, one_middle, etc)
        end
        
        Runtime->>Runtime: Validate required fields<br/>are present and non-empty
        
        alt All validations pass
            alt Streaming (level 2-3)
                Runtime->>ValidationExtractor: flush()
                ValidationExtractor-->>Client: Buffered content
            end
            Runtime->>Runtime: Remove validation code fields
            Runtime->>Runtime: Update success metrics
            Runtime-->>Client: Return parsed response
        else Validation fails
            alt Has retries remaining
                Runtime->>Runtime: Calculate backoff delay
                Runtime->>Runtime: Wait for backoff
                Note over Runtime: Loop continues with retry
            else No retries left
                Runtime->>Runtime: Update failure metrics
                Runtime-->>Client: Return null
            end
        end
    end
```

This PR transforms the MCP plugin architecture from a multi-step tool invocation pattern to native dynamic action registration, achieving significant performance improvements and code quality gains.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->a6:T3f51,# Summary

Rust WASM implementation for elizaOS v2.0.0 - enabling the Rust core to run in browser/Node.js environments via WebAssembly.

# Risks

**Low risk.** This PR:
- Makes no breaking API changes to existing Rust code
- Uses conditional compilation (`#[cfg]`) so native builds are unaffected
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Adds new WASM-specific code paths that only activate when building for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This PR makes the elizaOS Rust core **fully WASM-compatible**, enabling it to run in browsers and Node.js via WebAssembly. The existing Rust crate had WASM bindings but they were stubs - the `WasmAgentRuntime` was a placeholder that didn't actually wrap the real `AgentRuntime`.

The key challenge was that Rust's `async_trait` and many traits require `Send + Sync` bounds for thread-safety, but WASM is single-threaded and doesn't support these traits. This PR implements platform-aware macros and conditional compilation to provide the correct bounds for each target.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Platform-Aware Macros (`src/platform.rs`)

```rust
// Native: #[async_trait] (requires Send)
// WASM:   #[async_trait(?Send)] (no Send requirement)
platform_async_trait! {
    pub trait MyTrait { ... }
}

// Native: pub trait MyTrait: Send + Sync { ... }
// WASM:   pub trait MyTrait { ... }
define_platform_trait! {
    pub trait MyTrait { ... }
}
```

#### 2. Core Trait Migration

All core traits now compile for both targets:
- `ActionHandler`, `ProviderHandler`, `EvaluatorHandler`
- `DatabaseAdapter`, `Service`, `IAgentRuntime`
- Bootstrap traits: `Action`, `Provider`, `Evaluator`, `Service`

#### 3. Real WasmAgentRuntime

The `WasmAgentRuntime` now wraps the actual `AgentRuntime` using WASM-appropriate primitives:

```rust
pub struct WasmAgentRuntime {
    inner: Rc<RefCell<Option<AgentRuntime>>>,  // Not Arc - WASM is single-threaded
    character: RefCell<Character>,
    agent_id: UUID,
}
```

#### 4. Structured WASM Errors

Rich error objects for JavaScript consumers:

```rust
pub struct WasmError {
    pub code: String,      // "VALIDATION_ERROR", "RUNTIME_ERROR", etc.
    pub message: String,   // Human-readable message
    pub source: Option<String>,  // Field/component that caused error
}
```

#### 5. JavaScript Shims

Type-safe wrappers for JS callbacks:

```rust
pub struct JsModelHandler {
    js_object: JsValue,
    handle_func: Function,
}
```

#### 6. Bug Fix: ChannelType Serialization

Fixed `ChannelType` enum to serialize correctly:
- Before: `VoiceDm` → `"VOICEDM"` ❌
- After: `VoiceDm` → `"VOICE_DM"` ✅

## What kind of change is this?

- **Features** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- **Bug fixes** (ChannelType serialization)
- **Improvements** (structured errors, better WASM integration)

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes require a change to the project documentation:
- Added `examples/README.md` with usage instructions for native and WASM examples
- WASM module includes JSDoc comments for all exports

# Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

                              │
                              ▼

│                                                              │
│  Methods:                                                    │
│  - create(character_json) → WasmAgentRuntime                │
│  - initialize() → Promise<void>                             │
│  - handleMessage(msg_json) → Promise<response_json>         │
│  - registerModelHandler(type, JsModelHandler)               │
│  - stop()                                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

BaseDrizzleAdapter

    │         ▼                   ▼
    │   ┌──────────┐       ┌──────────┐
    │   │  Store1  │  ...  │  StoreN  │
    │   └──────────┘       └──────────┘
    │
    └── Public methods delegate to stores

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>


This PR adds a `CachedDatabaseAdapter` wrapper that provides LRU caching with optional external cache support (Redis/Upstash) for serverless environments, plus embedding dimension caching in the runtime to avoid redundant model calls.

**Key Changes:**
- New `CachedDatabaseAdapter` class implementing two-tier caching strategy (in-memory L1 + optional external L2)
- Runtime embedding dimension is now cached and can be pre-configured via `setEmbeddingDimension()`
- Automatic cache invalidation on mutations (updates, deletes, creates)
- Comprehensive test coverage (1,530 lines) covering all caching scenarios, TTL expiration, and external cache integration
- Smart invalidation strategy: individual entity caches are updated on mutation, while aggregate caches (like `entitiesForRoom`) are cleared

**Cache Strategy:**
- Read-through caching: Check L1 → L2 → Database, populating caches on miss
- Write-through invalidation: Mutations invalidate affected cache entries
- Configurable TTL per cache type with LRU eviction
- Memory operations (high volume) are NOT cached to avoid excessive memory usage

Also adds a broker-ready auth mode stub (not functional yet) so a future Eliza-hosted broker can be added without touching tweet logic.

This requires a “Twitter broker” I referenced below which is a future Eliza-hosted service (not implemented in this repo) that would sit between the plugin and Twitter to handle the parts that require a client secret and a user session.

What it is
A separate web service (owned by ElizaOS) that:
- Runs the OAuth2 “login + approve” flow on behalf of users
- Stores the client secret and refresh tokens securely
- Hands the agent/plugin short‑lived access tokens (so the plugin never needs secrets)


### What changed in this PR (exact)
- Introduced a single auth abstraction: TwitterAuthProvider#getAccessToken(): Promise<string>
- Added TWITTER_AUTH_MODE (env|oauth|broker) and centralized auth selection
- env mode (default): preserves TWITTER_API_KEY / TWITTER_API_SECRET_KEY / TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN / TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET behavior
- oauth mode: OAuth2 PKCE interactive login + token refresh + persistence
- broker mode: stub-only; fails clearly until an Eliza Twitter broker service exists
- Refactored TwitterAuth + client call sites to use provider-driven tokens (no direct env reads in request logic)
- Added unit tests for PKCE, OAuth2 refresh flows, token store, and broker stub
- Updated docs and plugin parameter metadata

### Auth modes
#### 1) Legacy env mode (no behavior change)
Set:
- TWITTER_AUTH_MODE=env (or omit)
- TWITTER_API_KEY
- TWITTER_API_SECRET_KEY
- TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN
- TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET

#### 2) OAuth2 PKCE mode ("login + approve")
Set:
- TWITTER_AUTH_MODE=oauth
- TWITTER_CLIENT_ID
- TWITTER_REDIRECT_URI (loopback recommended, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback)
Optional:
- TWITTER_SCOPES (default: tweet.read tweet.write users.read offline.access)

First run prints an authorization URL. After approval it stores tokens and auto-refreshes.

Requires a 

### Local callback server (required for best UX)
In oauth mode, the plugin starts a small local HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 to capture the OAuth redirect at the host/port/path in TWITTER_REDIRECT_URI.
- If it can’t bind, it falls back to "paste the redirected URL".

### Broker mode (stub; requires Eliza Twitter broker server)
If TWITTER_AUTH_MODE=broker:
- Requires TWITTER_BROKER_URL
- This PR does NOT implement the broker server; it only provides the plugin-side provider stub.
- Later, an Eliza-hosted broker (e.g. eliza twitter auth server) can hold the client secret and return short-lived access tokens.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->b2:T1b64,## Summary

Fixes shell environment variable leakage into ElizaOS plugin loading decisions and agent secrets.

**Problem:** `dotenv.config()` does NOT override existing `process.env` values by default. This means shell environment variables (from `.zshrc`/`.bashrc`) leak into plugin loading:

```
User shell has: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY
Project .env has: OPENROUTER_API_KEY

Expected plugins: openrouter, bootstrap
Actual plugins: anthropic, openai, openrouter, bootstrap (LEAKED!)
```

**Solution:**
- Scan installed plugins for declared env vars via `package.json` `agentConfig.pluginParameters`
- Set global filter so only declared vars are captured into agent secrets
- Load `.env` files with proper precedence (closest file wins)

## Changes

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-env-filter.ts`** - New utility to scan plugins for env var declarations
- **`packages/core/src/secrets.ts`** - Add `setAllowedEnvVars()` filter to restrict captured vars
- **`packages/core/src/utils/environment.ts`** - Add `loadEnvFilesWithPrecedence()` for proper hierarchy
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/start/index.ts`** - Integrate filter before character loading

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for plugin env var scanning (`plugin-env-filter.test.ts`)
- [x] Unit tests for secrets filtering (`secrets-filtering.test.ts`)
- [x] Unit tests for env precedence loading (`env-precedence.test.ts`)
- [ ] Manual test with shell env vars vs project .env
- [ ] Test in monorepo context

## Notes

- 40 tests passing
- Backwards compatible (null filter = existing behavior)
- Core env vars (POSTGRES_URL, LOG_LEVEL, etc.) always allowed

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

### Greptile Summary

This PR implements a robust solution to prevent shell environment variable leakage into ElizaOS agent secrets by introducing plugin-based environment variable filtering.

## Key Changes

- **Plugin Environment Scanning**: New `plugin-env-filter.ts` utility scans installed plugins' `package.json` files for declared environment variables via `agentConfig.pluginParameters`
- **Global Filter in Secrets Module**: Added `setAllowedEnvVars()` to restrict which environment variables are captured into agent secrets
- **Environment File Precedence**: New `loadEnvFilesWithPrecedence()` ensures closest `.env` file wins, respecting monorepo boundaries
- **Integration in Start Command**: Filter is applied before character loading, preventing shell vars from leaking into plugin selection

## Architecture

The solution follows a clear flow: scan plugins → set filter → load env files → filter on capture. Core environment variables (e.g., `POSTGRES_URL`, `LOG_LEVEL`) are always allowed. The filter is null by default for backward compatibility.

## Issues Found

- Line 72 in `plugin-env-filter.ts` already correctly checks for null declarations before accessing length
- Line 19 in `secrets.ts` uses underscore variable as TypeScript idiom for unused loop variable (valid pattern)
- Consider caching regex compilation in `detectShellOnlyVars` for performance
- `CORE_ALLOWED_VARS` hardcoded in CLI could be centralized in core package

## Testing

40 tests passing across 3 new test files with comprehensive coverage of filtering, precedence, and integration scenarios.

### Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge with minor considerations
- The implementation is well-tested with 40 passing tests, addresses a real security concern (shell env leakage), and maintains backward compatibility. Code quality is high with proper error handling and optimization. Minor issues include hardcoded core vars list and potential for regex caching, but these don't affect functionality.
- Pay close attention to `packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-env-filter.ts` for the regex caching optimization and consider centralizing `CORE_ALLOWED_VARS`

</ul>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.2</h2>
<h3>Bug fixes</h3>
<ul>
<li>Fixed relations extraction to not interfere with Drizzle Studio.</li>
</ul>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.1</h2>
<h3>Fixed <code>drizzle-kit pull</code> bugs when using Gel extensions.</h3>
<p>Because Gel extensions create schema names containing <code>::</code> (for example, <code>ext::auth</code>), Drizzle previously handled these names incorrectly. Starting with this release, you can use Gel extensions without any problems. Here’s what you should do:</p>
<ol>
<li>Enable extensions schemas in <code>drizzle.config.ts</code></li>
</ol>
<pre lang="ts"><code>import  { defineConfig } from &quot;drizzle-kit&quot;;
<p>export default defineConfig({
dialect: 'gel',
schemaFilter: ['ext::auth', 'public']
});
</code></pre></p>
<ol start="2">
<li>
<p>Run <code>drizzle-kit pull</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Done!</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h2>drizzle-kit@0.31.0</h2>
<h2>Features and improvements</h2>
<h3>Enum DDL improvements</h3>
<!-- raw HTML omitted -->

<pre lang="tsx"><code>// Input
type Foo = (/** comment */ a | b) | c;
<p>// Prettier 3.7.3
type Foo = /** comment <em>/ (/</em>* comment */ a | b) | c;</p>
<p>// Prettier 3.7.4
type Foo = /** comment */ (a | b) | c;
</code></pre></p>

  // comment

);
<p>// Prettier 3.7.3 (first format)
type X = (A | B) &amp;
(// comment
A | B);</p>
<p>// Prettier 3.7.3 (second format)
type X = (
| A
&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;
</code></pre></p>

Updates `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` from 0.6.14 to 0.7.2
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/releases">prettier-plugin-tailwindcss's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>v0.7.2</h2>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Load compatible plugins sequentially to work around race conditions in Node.js (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/412">#412</a>)</li>
<li>Fix compatibility with <code>prettier-plugin-svelte</code> when using Prettier v3.7+ (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/418">#418</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2>v0.7.1</h2>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Match against correct name of dynamic attributes when using regexes (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/410">#410</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h2>v0.7.0</h2>
<h3>Added</h3>
<ul>
<li>Format quotes in <code>@source</code>, <code>@plugin</code>, and <code>@config</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/387">#387</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in function calls in Twig (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/358">#358</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in callable template literals (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/367">#367</a>)</li>
<li>Sort in function calls mixed with property accesses (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/367">#367</a>)</li>
<li>Support regular expression patterns for attributes (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/405">#405</a>)</li>
<li>Support regular expression patterns for function names (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/405">#405</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h3>Changed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Improved monorepo support by loading Tailwind CSS relative to the input file instead of prettier config file (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/386">#386</a>)</li>
<li>Improved monorepo support by loading v3 configs relative to the input file instead of prettier config file (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/386">#386</a>)</li>
<li>Fallback to Tailwind CSS v4 instead of v3 by default (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/390">#390</a>)</li>
<li>Don't augment global Prettier <code>ParserOptions</code> and <code>RequiredOptions</code> types (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/354">#354</a>)</li>
<li>Drop support for <code>prettier-plugin-import-sort</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/385">#385</a>)</li>
</ul>
<h3>Fixed</h3>
<ul>
<li>Handle quote escapes in LESS when sorting <code>@apply</code> (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/392">#392</a>)</li>
<li>Fix whitespace removal inside nested concat and template expressions (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/tailwindlabs/prettier-plugin-tailwindcss/pull/396">#396</a>)</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
</details>

<h3>Patch Changes</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p><a href="https://redirect.github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/pull/1523">#1523</a> <a href="https://github.com/eyaltoledano/claude-task-master/commit/fc1a79f2565b0d8c24f009aec2c473a335262ae2"><code>fc1a79f</code></a> Thanks <a href="https://github.com/Crunchyman-ralph"><code>@​Crunchyman-ralph</code></a>! - Codex cli Validate reasoning effort against model capabilities</p>

</li>

<!-- /greptile_comment -->b5:T1832,## Summary

Add **BlockRun plugin** enabling ElizaOS agents to make pay-per-request AI calls using [x402 micropayments](https://x402.org) on Base chain.

- **BLOCKRUN_CHAT** action: Pay-per-request access to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and more
- **BLOCKRUN_WALLET** provider: Wallet address and USDC balance on Base
- Automatic x402 payment handling via EIP-712 signatures
- No API keys required - just a wallet with USDC

## How it works

1. Agent makes an AI request via `BLOCKRUN_CHAT` action
2. BlockRun gateway returns `402 Payment Required` with price
3. Plugin signs USDC payment (EIP-712 TransferWithAuthorization)
4. Request retries with payment signature
5. AI response returned to agent

Typical cost: **$0.001-0.01 per request**

## Configuration

```env
BASE_CHAIN_WALLET_KEY=0x...  # Private key with USDC on Base
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { blockrunPlugin } from '@elizaos/plugin-blockrun';

const agent = new Agent({
  plugins: [blockrunPlugin],
});
```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for plugin exports
- [x] Wallet provider returns address and balance
- [x] Action validates wallet configuration
- [x] E2E test with real x402 payments (3 successful API calls)

## Links

- [BlockRun](https://blockrun.ai) - Pay-per-request AI gateway
- [x402 Protocol](https://x402.org) - HTTP 402 micropayment standard
- [@blockrun/llm SDK](https://github.com/BlockRunAI/blockrun-llm-ts)

<h2>Greptile Overview</h2>

### Greptile Summary

This PR adds a BlockRun plugin that enables ElizaOS agents to make pay-per-request AI calls using the x402 micropayment protocol on Base chain. The plugin provides a `BLOCKRUN_CHAT` action for making AI API calls and a `BLOCKRUN_WALLET` provider for wallet context.

## What Changed

The PR introduces a complete plugin package (`@elizaos/plugin-blockrun`) with:
- **Action**: `BLOCKRUN_CHAT` - handles AI requests with automatic x402 payment flow
- **Provider**: `BLOCKRUN_WALLET` - supplies wallet address and USDC balance on Base
- **Dependencies**: Uses `@blockrun/llm` SDK for payment handling and `viem` for blockchain interactions
- **Tests**: Comprehensive unit and E2E tests validating the payment flow

## Architecture

The plugin follows ElizaOS patterns with proper action/provider structure:
1. User sends message to agent
2. Action validates wallet configuration
3. LLMClient makes request to BlockRun gateway
4. Gateway returns 402 Payment Required with price
5. Client signs USDC payment via EIP-712
6. Request retries with payment signature
7. AI response returned to agent

## Key Implementation Details

- **Client Caching**: LLMClient instances are cached per agent ID to avoid recreating connections
- **Wallet Configuration**: Supports `BASE_CHAIN_WALLET_KEY` and `BLOCKRUN_WALLET_KEY` settings
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive try-catch blocks with structured logging
- **Model Support**: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google models via unified interface

## Critical Issues Found

1. **Hardcoded Path** (test-e2e.ts:9): Import uses absolute local path that breaks for other developers
2. **Missing LICENSE**: Package.json references LICENSE file not included in PR
3. **Git Dependency**: Uses git URL instead of published npm package for @blockrun/llm

## Code Quality

The code is well-structured with:
- Proper TypeScript typing throughout
- Good error handling and logging
- Clear documentation and examples
- Comprehensive test coverage including real payment flows
- Follows ElizaOS plugin architecture patterns

### Confidence Score: 3/5

- This PR has good functionality but contains a critical bug that breaks builds for other developers
- Score reflects one critical syntax error (hardcoded local path) that will cause immediate build failures, plus two medium-priority issues (missing LICENSE file and git dependency). The core implementation is solid with proper error handling, validation, and comprehensive tests. Once the hardcoded path is fixed, this would be a 4/5.
- test-e2e.ts requires immediate fix for hardcoded path. package.json needs LICENSE file added and consideration of publishing @blockrun/llm to npm.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->b6:Te20,## Summary

Implements field-level encryption for sensitive database credentials (`user_database_uri`) using AES-256-GCM with per-organization Data Encryption Keys (DEKs).

- **Per-organization encryption keys** for tenant isolation
- **Encoded format** (`enc:v1:...`) requires zero schema changes
- **Backward compatible**: handles both encrypted and legacy plaintext URIs
- **Migration script** for encrypting existing data

## Architecture

```
Master Key (SECRETS_MASTER_KEY env var)
    └── wraps →
Organization DEKs (stored encrypted in DB)
    └── encrypts →
Sensitive fields (user_database_uri, future: API keys, etc.)
```

**Encrypted format**: `enc:v1:<org_key_id>:<nonce>:<auth_tag>:<ciphertext>`

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `lib/services/field-encryption.ts` | Core encryption service (AES-256-GCM) |
| `db/schemas/organization-encryption-keys.ts` | Drizzle schema for org encryption keys |
| `db/repositories/organization-encryption-keys.ts` | Repository for CRUD operations |
| `db/migrations/0017_add_organization_encryption_keys.sql` | Schema migration |
| `lib/services/user-database.ts` | Encrypt URI on store, add decrypt helper |
| `lib/services/sandbox/tool-executor.ts` | Decrypt URI before injecting as DATABASE_URL |
| `scripts/migrate-encrypt-user-database-uris.ts` | Migration script for existing data |
| `example.env.local` | Documentation for new env vars |

## Deployment Checklist

- [ ] Run migration `0017_add_organization_encryption_keys.sql`
- [ ] **Add `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY` to Vercel Environment Variables**
  - Generate with: `openssl rand -hex 32`
  - Must be 64 hex characters (32 bytes)
  - ⚠️ Back up securely - losing this key means losing access to encrypted data
- [ ] Deploy code changes
- [ ] Run migration script: `npx tsx scripts/migrate-encrypt-user-database-uris.ts`
- [ ] Verify no plaintext URIs remain

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify new database provisioning encrypts the URI
- [ ] Verify sandbox tool executor correctly decrypts and injects DATABASE_URL
- [ ] Verify migration script encrypts existing plaintext URIs
- [ ] Verify backward compatibility with any remaining plaintext URIs (logs warning)

<!-- /greptile_comment -->b8:T1e68,## Summary

Optimize `runtime.initialize()` performance through atomic upserts and parallelization of independent operations.

**Results:** Cold start -30%, Warm start -40%

## Problem

The current initialization flow has several inefficiencies:
1. Sequential check-then-insert patterns with race condition potential
2. Multiple round-trips to DB for existence checks before inserts
3. Sequential operations that could run in parallel

## Solution

### 1. Atomic Upserts (plugin-sql/base.ts)

Replace check-then-insert with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`:

```typescript
// Before: Two queries + race condition
const existing = await this.getWorld(world.id);
if (existing) throw new Error('World already exists');
await this.db.insert(worldTable).values(world);

// After: Single atomic query
await this.db.insert(worldTable).values(world).onConflictDoNothing();
```

Applied to:
- `createWorld()` - returns silently if world exists
- `createEntities()` - skips existing entities in batch

### 2. Parallel Initialization (core/runtime.ts)

```typescript
// Before: Sequential
await this.ensureWorldExists();
await this.runMigrations();
const entity = await this.getEntityById(entityId);
const room = await this.getRoomById(roomId);

// After: Parallel where possible
await Promise.all([
  this.ensureWorldExists(),
  options?.skipMigrations ? Promise.resolve() : this.runMigrations()
]);

const [entity, room] = await Promise.all([
  this.getEntityById(entityId),
  this.getRoomById(roomId)
]);
```

### 3. Idempotent Ensure Methods

- `ensureWorldExists()` - Always calls `createWorld()`, DB handles duplicates
- `ensureRoomExists()` - Always calls `createRoom()`, DB handles duplicates
- `ensureEntity()` - New method using upsert pattern

### 4. Code Cleanup (server/message.ts)

Removed defensive try/catch blocks that were handling race conditions no longer possible with atomic upserts.

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `packages/plugin-sql/src/base.ts` | Added `onConflictDoNothing()` to createWorld, createEntities |
| `packages/core/src/runtime.ts` | Parallel init, extracted `mergeAgentSettings()`, added `ensureEntity()` |
| `packages/server/src/services/message.ts` | Removed unnecessary try/catch blocks |
| `packages/*/src/__tests__/**` | Updated tests for idempotent behavior |

## Benchmark Details

```
Environment: PGLite (in-memory), 20 iterations each

=== COLD START (fresh DB each time) ===
Delta:  -30%

=== WARM START (agent already exists) ===
Delta:  -40%
```

- [x] `bun test packages/plugin-sql/src/__tests__/integration/` - All suites pass
